The victim, 19-year-old Jaden Batista, was rushed to the hospital where she ultimately succumbed to her wounds. According to reports, Batista suffered approximately 15 stab wounds to the neck and chest. Despite officers arriving as the attack was happening, the injuries were catastrophic. The murder weapon, a blood-stained knife, was recovered on scene. The suspect, 23-year-old Trevor Weigel, was taken to the hospital for a stab wound to his own neck, but ultimately survived. He was later charged with first-degree murder, burglary, criminal attempted kidnapping, possession of an instrument of crime, unlawful restraint, evading arrest, false imprisonment, disorderly conduct, and a summary count of harassment. The case proceeded to trial in January 26, where Trevor maintained his innocence, resulting in a lengthy contested trial before the jury. According to the Bucks County District Attorney's Office, jurors heard testimony and reviewed evidence throughout the week. It took them just over an hour to reach a verdict. Prosecutors argued that the killing was a premeditated act, triggered by Batista ending their brief relationship. In the weeks leading up to the attack, Trevor had sent Jaden unsettling drawings, even confronting her about why she never responded to them. That behavior, prosecutors said, reflected a growing fixation. Deputy District Attorney A.J. Garabedian told jurors that Weigel became consumed by rage and obsession after Batista blocked his phone number and social media accounts. As Garibetian stated in court, if he couldn't have her, nobody was going to have her, and he made sure of it. The jury found Weigel guilty on all major counts, including first-degree murder. And on April 28, 26, the now 25-year-old Trevor Weigel was sentenced to a mandatory term of life in prison without the possibility of parole.
